newsitem.title: USA: Valspar, Ameron to swap assets.
newsitem.headline: Valspar, Ameron to swap assets.

text.p: Valspar Corp, which makes coatings, said Monday it signed an agreement with Ameron International Corp to exchange certain assets of Valspar's maintenance coatings division for selected assets of the product finishes business of Ameron.
Sales of Valspar's business were about $18 million in 1996, and the Ameron businesses had $16 million of sales last year.
The transaction is expected to be finalized within the next 60 days, and terms were not disclosed, Valspar said in a statement.
The Product Finishes business includes both liquid and powder industrial coatings. No facilities are included in the exchange.
Valspar said it will remain in the Marine Coatings and Functional Powder Coatings businesses.

In a related action, Valspar said that it will close its plant in Beaumont, Texas, which primarily produces coatings for the Maintenance division. Marine coatings production at the facility will be moved to the company's plant in Garland, Texas.

About 40 people are currently employed at the Beaumont plant, and some of the employees will be offered transfers to Valspar's Garland plant. Costs of the closure were recognized in the first quarter.

Richard Rompala, Valspar president and chief executive officer, said, "The closure of the Beaumont facility is another step in our drive to increase efficiency and rationalize production. In addition, the swap with Ameron enables both companies to strengthen core businesses."
